- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Tyrannosaurus Rex roamed North America during the Late Cretaceous period, around 68-65 million years ago.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] T-Rex's habitat was likely a mix of forests, rivers, and coastal areas, with a subtropical to temperate climate.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] T-Rex was an apex predator with exceptional eyesight, powerful legs, and a formidable bite force.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] T-Rex had the strongest bite of any dinosaur, with a force of around 6-9 tons per square inch (psi).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Fossil evidence suggests that T-Rex had feathers, which might have been used for display or insulation.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] T-Rex might have used ambush tactics for hunting and likely scavenged carrion.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] There is evidence suggesting T-Rex might have lived in small family groups.
- [FACT] The user expressed interest in learning about other dinosaurs that co-existed with the T-Rex.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Notable herbivorous dinosaurs that co-existed with T-Rex include Edmontosaurus, Triceratops, Ankylosaurus, Styracosaurus, and Hadrosaurus.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Edmontosaurus could grow up to 12 meters (40 feet) in length and had a distinctive crest on its head.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Triceratops had three horns and a frill on its head, likely used for display or defense.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Ankylosaurus was an armored dinosaur with a club-like tail for defense.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Styracosaurus had a frill adorned with long spikes and was around 5-6 meters (16-20 feet) long.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Hadrosaurus was around 6-8 meters (20-26 feet) long and had a distinctive crest on its head.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Other dinosaurs from the same period include Daspletosaurus, Gorgosaurus, and Ornithomimus.
